name: Isolated Duodenal Duplication

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic or tubular structure contiguous with the duodenum
Histological confirmation of a smooth muscle layer in the cyst wall
Presence of duodenal or gastrointestinal mucosal lining within the cyst
Characteristic imaging findings on ultrasound, CT, or MRI showing duplication cyst
Symptoms such as abdominal pain or vomiting suggestive of duodenal obstruction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a cystic structure contiguous with the duodenum with histological confirmation of smooth muscle layer and mucosal lining
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed postoperatively by histopathology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Duodenal obstruction due to cystic mass effect
pathognomonic.notes: Leads to vomiting and feeding intolerance in infants

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable abdominal mass in the epigastric region
searchTerms: abdominal mass felt in epigastric area

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain localized to the upper abdomen
Feeding intolerance in neonates or infants

common.notes: Due to obstruction or communication with pancreatic ducts

occasional.notes: From ectopic gastric mucosa causing ulceration

occasional.symptomName: Infection or abscess formation within the cyst

rare.symptomName: Malignant transformation within the duplication cyst
rare.notes: Extremely rare but reported in literature

rare.symptomName: Anaphylactic reaction due to cyst rupture
searchTerms: severe allergic reaction from cyst rupture
life-threatening allergy due to cyst rupture

laboratory: Elevated amylase and lipase in cases with pancreatitis
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic lesion adjacent to duodenum
CT/MRI demonstrating cystic mass with characteristic wall and possible communication with duodenum
Endoscopic ultrasound may show duplication cyst features
other: Histopathology confirming smooth muscle layer and mucosal lining consistent with duodenal duplication

distinguishingFeatures: Cystic dilation of bile ducts rather than duplication of duodenum
Lack of smooth muscle and mucosal lining
Usually located within or adjacent to pancreas
Cyst located within mesentery, not contiguous with duodenum

redFlags: Signs of bowel obstruction such as persistent vomiting and abdominal distension
Acute abdomen indicating cyst rupture or infection
references: Stringer MD. Duplication cysts. Clin Radiol. 2006;61(7): 555-565.
Puligandla PS, et al. Gastrointestinal duplications. J Pediatr Surg. 2003;38(5):740-744.
